hints.title: Duplicate Minimum Ambiguity
hints.text: When nums[mid] equals nums[right], the minimum could lie on either side of midpoint. Which single index can you discard without losing any viable candidate?

hints.title: Right Boundary Pruning Invariant
hints.text: If nums[mid] == nums[right], decrement right by 1 since nums[mid] preserves the value. If nums[mid] < nums[right], min is at or left of mid; if nums[mid] > nums[right], min is strictly right.

hints.title: Adaptive Convergence Procedure
hints.text: Initialize left = 0, right = len(nums) - 1. While left < right, let mid = (left + right) // 2. If nums[mid] > nums[right], set left = mid + 1. If nums[mid] < nums[right], set right = mid. Otherwise right -= 1. Return nums[left].

hints.title: Complete Implementation

variables: N: length of nums array (1 <= N <= 5000)
complexity.notes: Logarithmic inflection search safely pruning right pointer on flat duplicate values.
complexity.whyNaiveFails: Identical elements at boundaries prevent knowing whether the inflection step is left or right.
complexity.interviewerExpectation: Using nums[mid] vs nums[right] rather than nums[left] to maintain correct invariant when array is already sorted.
